newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Oil Search outlines Moran development.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Oil Search outlines Moran development.

text.p: Oil explorer and producer Oil Search Ltd said on Monday its Moran oil field in Papua New Guinea could start producing 10,000 barrels of oil per day as early as September this year.

Oil Search managing director Peter Botten told an analysts briefing the field, which first reported good drilling reports last November, was considered commercial even though oil had been confirmed in only one area of the structure.
The first stage of planned development was an extended well test using the Moran-1X and 2X wells, designed primarily to get reservoir and production information, Botten said.
"But obviously it will provide a cash flow," he added.
Operators would use spare capacity at the nearby Agogo production facility, which was currently 10,000 barrels of oil per day (bpd), but could increase to 20,000 bpd.
Botten said capital equipment worth US$34 million for the development had been ordered, and discussions with landowners were fairly well advanced.
The first phase of full development would involve the drilling of the planned Moran-3X and 4X wells to build a critical mass of reserves by the end of 1997.
Production from Moran-1X and 2X should rise to 30,000 bpd by the first quarter of 1998, with other wells expected to add to production.
"Should the results of drilling work we should see full field development by the end of the third quarter of 1999," Botten said.
Flow rates would depend on the size of the reservoir and the extent of fields to the north-west and south-east, but operators were working on a run of 120,000 bpd, he said.

Botten warned the reservoir needed to be proven, but said the initial estimation of reserves was substantially higher than the nearby Kutubu field, which has recoverable reserves of about 305 million barrels.
Landowner expectations also needed to be met, while operators would have to apply for two further production licences.

Oil Search has 7.76 percent of the PDL-2 licence containing Moran-1X and 2X. Other participants include operator Chevron Corp, The Broken Hill Pty Co Ltd, British Petroleum Co Plc, Mobil Corp and Orogen Minerals Ltd.
Botten said the Moran field was believed to straddle three permits.
Talks were under way about re-structuring holdings of the field and needed to be completed by the third quarter of 1998 under the current timetable.
Oil Search shares were 10 cents lower at A$2.55 at 3.15 p.m. (0415 GMT) on Monday.
